considered_because: Passes the policy screen: Annex I strategic ("silicon metal") and the wafer of PV, c-Si, which Carrara 2020 Table 4 gives at 4000 kg/MW.
reason: Held out deliberately. Silicon's constraint is polysilicon refining capacity, not the ore — quartz is abundant — so a mine-production supply side of the kind this study builds would not measure it. Bieuville's shortage screen agrees (0.020, well under any threshold tested).

considered_because: Passes the policy screen: Annex I strategic ("boron — metallurgy grade") and the B of NdFeB. Also bought as the SOEC electrolyte's boric oxide, 6.4 kg/MW.
reason: Held out deliberately. Boron is the one policy-screen metal the shortage screen rejects outright: Bieuville puts energy-led demand at 1.4e-05 of primary capacity, four orders of magnitude below the next metal, because borates are abundant and a magnet is ~1% boron by mass. Including it would add a row that can only ever sit at the origin of Fig. 2b.

considered_because: Bought as the tower galvanising of all four wind sub-technologies, 5500 kg/MW in Carrara 2020 Table 2.
reason: On neither screen: not a CRMA raw material, 0.019 on the shortage screen. Kept as a Helper row in data/mineral_info.csv because germanium's supply is derived from its host ratio to zinc, but it is not a demand target.

considered_because: Passes the policy screen: Annex I strategic ("titanium metal") and the PEM bipolar plate, which Gerloff 2021 gives at 528 kg/MW.
reason: Held out deliberately, on silicon's reasoning. Titanium's constraint is sponge and melting capacity, not the ore — ilmenite and rutile are abundant and mined at many times the metal's output — so a mine-production supply side of the kind this study builds would not measure it. It is also outside Bieuville's 32, so no shortage figure exists to weigh against that.

considered_because: Bought as the SOEC blocking layer's ceria, 91.5 kg/MW in Gerloff 2021.
reason: On neither screen: the Annex I wording covers cerium among the "rare earth elements for permanent magnets", and a solid-oxide blocking layer is not one, so the entry does not designate it; and cerium is outside Bieuville's 32. It is the most abundant rare earth and a surplus co-product of neodymium separation, so it is not what binds.

considered_because: Bought as the SOEC's zirconia at 170.7 kg/MW and the AEC's Zirfon diaphragm at 73 kg/MW, in Gerloff 2021.
reason: On neither screen: not a CRMA raw material, and 1.4e-08 on the shortage screen — the transition barely touches it. Zircon is an abundant co-product of the titanium-mineral sands.

considered_because: Bought as the SOEC electrolyte's barium oxide, 6.4 kg/MW in Gerloff 2021.
reason: On neither screen: baryte is on Annex II as critical only, which this screen does not admit (as for niobium), and barium is outside Bieuville's 32. 6.4 kg/MW sits against 25 t/MW of steel in the same stack.
